'''Bruce Alexander Fuhrer''' [[Order of Australia|OAM]] (31 December 1930 – 31 March 2023) was an Australian botanist and photographer, specialising in cryptogams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fungi Photographer|url=http://www.adm.monash.edu.au/records-archives/archives/cgi-alias/monpix?Disp_PHOTOGRAPH_DATE=1&Disp_IMAGE_NUMBER=1&Disp_IMAGE_TITLE=1&Disp_Cols=2&IMAGE_NUMBER=480&SUBJECT_DESCRIPTOR=Botany|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> His photographic collection of fungi numbers more than 3000 species.

==Early life==
Born in [[Woollahra, New South Wales|Woollahra]], Sydney, in 1930, Fuhrer developed his interest in nature as a boy, exploring the parks and forests of Sydney and the [[Blue Mountains (New South Wales)|Blue Mountains]] with his father. At 17, Fuhrer moved to [[Portland, Victoria]]. Fuhrer met and was inspired by local naturalists Oswald Lightbody (Ossie) and [[Alexander Clifford Beauglehole]] (Cliff). It was during this period that he developed his interest in [[natural history]] and joined the Portland Field Naturalists' Club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cohn |first=Helen |title=Fuhrer, Bruce Alexander |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P007385b.htm |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation |language=en-gb}}</ref>

==Career==
Fuhrer began his career as a photographer in Portland in 1955. In 1957 he formed the Portland Camera Club and was its president for six years. He was an inaugural member of the [[Mount Richmond National Park]] Management Committee, formed in 1960. He joined the [[Field Naturalists Club of Victoria]] (FNCV) and the [[Ringwood Field Naturalists Club]] in the sixties, and became Chairman of the Botany Group of the FNCV for three years.<ref>{{Cite book |last= |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/178977 |title=The Victorian Naturalist - Field Naturalists' Club of Victoria. |date=1967 |publisher=Field Naturalists Club of Victoria - Hosted by the Biodiversity Heritage Library |volume=v.84 (1967) |location=[Melbourne]}}</ref> He also served on the FNCV Council between 1964 and 1968. In 1961 Fuhrer established the Ringwood Junior Field Naturalist Club<ref>{{cite web|title=Ringwood Junior Field Naturalists Club|url=https://rfnc.org.au/history.html}}</ref> and was president for sixteen years of its existence. He later established 'The Basin Junior Field Naturalist' Club<ref>{{cite web|title=The Basin Field Naturalist' Club|url=http://www.coxhill.com/basinhistory/organisations/Voluntary%20Organisations.pdf}}</ref> (now the Wildlife Observers Club Inc.) Fuhrer contributed substantial photographs in the first comprehensive illustrative guide to Victorian Flora – ''Flowers And Plants Of Victoria And Tasmania'' published in 1968. Already acknowledged as a botanist and photographer, he was invited to judge at the 1970, 1974 and 1978 Victorian Photoflora Competitions.

Fuhrer's first publication was in 1978: ''A Field Guide to the Common Genera of Gilled Fungi in Australia''. He subsequently wrote many books on Australian fungi, including ''A Field Guide to Australian Fungi''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Fuhrer|first=Bruce|title=A Field Guide to Australian Fungi|year=2005|location=Melbourne|isbn=9781876473518|pages=360|url=https://www.publish.csiro.au/pid/5024.htm}}</ref> Fuhrer worked for 25 years in the School of Biology at [[Monash University]]. At this time, he co-authored species including ''Rozites armeniacovelatus'' (now ''[[Cortinarius armeniacovelatus]]'').<ref>{{cite web|title=Rozites armeniacovelatus|url=http://www.mycobank.org/BioloMICS.aspx?TableKey=14682616000000067&Rec=191301&Fields=All|website=Mycobank|access-date=2 June 2016}}</ref> For this work at [[Monash University]], he received an Honorary Master of Science degree<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary Master of Science degree|url=http://www.adm.monash.edu.au/records-archives/archives/cgi-alias/monpix?Disp_PHOTOGRAPH_DATE=CHECKED&Disp_DIMENSIONS=&IMAGE_TITLE=fuhrer&Submit=Search&Disp_NOTES=&IMAGE_NUMBER=1309&Disp_MEDIA=&PHOTOGRAPH_DATE=&Disp_IMAGE_NUMBER=CHECKED&PHOTOGRAPHER=&Disp_SUBJECT_DESCRIPTOR=&Disp_IMAGE_TITLE=CHECKED&APT_TOPIC=&Disp_Cols=2&Disp_PHOTOGRAPHER=&Disp_COLOUR_BW=|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> in 1988. Fuhrer was a Senior Technical Officer, Departments of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, at Monash University for the years 1972 to 1996. Fuhrer has discovered several previously undescribed fungal species and described many [[liverworts]]. There are four species of fungi and two [[liverworts]] named after Fuhrer. The fungi are ''[[Calostoma fuhreri]]''<ref>{{cite web|title=Calostoma fuhreri|url=http://www.mycobank.org/Biolomics.aspx?Table=Mycobank&MycoBankNr_=103115|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> (desert prettymouth), ''[[Hygrocybe fuhreri]]'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Hygrocybe fuhreri|url=http://www.mycobank.org/Biolomics.aspx?Table=Mycobank&MycoBankNr_=482862|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> ''[[Hypoxylon fuhreri]]''<ref>{{cite web|title=Hypoxylon fuhreri|url=http://www.mycobank.org/Biolomics.aspx?Table=Mycobank&MycoBankNr_=460009|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> and ''[[Mycena fuhreri]]'';<ref>{{cite web|title=Mycena fuhreri|url=http://www.mycobank.org/Biolomics.aspx?Table=Mycobank&MycoBankNr_=489671|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> the [[liverworts]] are ''[[Fossombronia fuhreri]]''<ref>{{cite web|title=Fossombronia fuhreri|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/35203242|access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> and ''[[Bazzania fuhreri]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bazzania fuhreri|url=https://herbarium.univie.ac.at/database/detail.php?ID=255661}}</ref>

==Death==
Fuhrer died on 31 March 2023, at the age of 92.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cairnspost.com.au/tributes/notice/death-notices/fuhrer-bruce-alexander-oam/6044089/ | title=Fuhrer, Bruce Alexander (OAM) &#124; Death Notices &#124; Melbourne }}</ref>

==Publications==
Books authored by Fuhrer, or in collaboration with others:
* 2010 A Field Guide to Australian Fungi (Revised edition) {{ISBN|9781876473518}} 
* 2009 (With M Corrick) Wildflowers of southern Western Australia. 3rd Edition {{ISBN|9781877058844}}
* 2003 Field Guide to the [[Mosses]] and Allied Plants of Southern Australia, David Meagher and Bruce Fuhrer (Flora of Australia Supplementary Series No. 20) {{ISBN|9780642568281}}
* 2002 Wildflowers of Southern Western Australia, Margaret G. Corrick and Bruce A. Fuhrer {{ISBN|9781877058844}}
* 2001 Australian Fungi: A Field Companion {{ISBN|9781876473402}}
* 2001 Wildflowers of Victoria, Margaret G. Corrick and Bruce A. Fuhrer {{ISBN|9781876473143}}
* 1992 Rainforest Fungi of Tasmania and South-East Australia, Bruce A. Fuhrer and Richard Robinson {{ISBN|9780643052413}}
* 1988 [[Seaweeds]] of Australia, text edited by Iona G. Christianson, Margaret N. Clayton and Bruce M. Allender {{ISBN|9780589502935}}
* 1985 A Field Companion To Australian Fungi {{ISBN|0867880635}}<ref>{{cite news |url=https://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article122525695 |title=A field guide to Australian fungi |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |volume=59 |issue=18,232 |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=31 August 1985 |accessdate=6 March 2024 |page=18 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref>
* 1984 A Field Guide to The Common Genera Of Gilled Fungi in Australia (Mushrooms and Toadstools) Martina Cole, Bruce A. Fuhrer and Albert Holland, Revised edition {{ISBN|9780909605117}}
* 1980 Flowers And Plants Of Victoria And Tasmania, Gordon R. Cochrane, Bruce A. Fuhrer, Edward R. Rotherham, John Simmons, Marion Simmons, [[James Hamlyn Willis]], Revised edition {{ISBN|9780589502560}}

==Awards==
* 2011 [[Order of Australia]] Medal [[Order of Australia|OAM]]
* 2009 Andrew Gibson Nature Medallion<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Gibson Nature Medallion|url=http://www.a-p-s.org.au/index.php/nature-medallion|access-date=1 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502054422/http://www.a-p-s.org.au/index.php/nature-medallion|archive-date=2 May 2014}}</ref> from the Australian Photographic Society Inc.
* 2005 Life member of [[Field Naturalists Club of Victoria]] (FNCV)
* 1995–1998 Honorary Associate, National Herbarium of Victoria, Royal Botanic Gardens Melbourne
* 1995 Honorary [[Research Associate]], Departments of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, [[Monash University]]
* 1989 [[Australian Natural History Medallion]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Australian Natural History Medallion |url=http://www.fncv.org.au/wp-content/themes/field-naturalist/publications/ANHM/ANHM_WINNERSs.pdf |access-date=1 May 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502003339/http://www.fncv.org.au/wp-content/themes/field-naturalist/publications/ANHM/ANHM_WINNERSs.pdf |archive-date=2 May 2014 }}</ref> from the [[Field Naturalists Club of Victoria]] (FNCV)
* 1988 Honorary Master of Science degree, [[Monash University]]
* 1976 Life member of [[Ringwood Field Naturalists Club]] Inc.
